ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, rectangle OABC is divided into six smaller rectangles by three lines. If D and E are the trisection points on the side CO, and the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{k}{x}\left(k\ne 0\right)$ just passes through the vertices F, G of the smaller rectangles. If the area of the shaded rectangles in the figure $S_{1}+S_{2}=5$, then what is the value of the inverse proportionality constant $k$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textit{Solution}: Since D and E are the trisection points on side CO, \\
it follows that $S_{1}+S_{2}=\frac{1}{3}S_{\text{rectangle} OABC}$, \\
hence $S_{\text{rectangle} OAGD}=\frac{2}{3}S_{\text{rectangle} OABC}$, \\
therefore $S_{\text{rectangle} OAGD}=2(S_{1}+S_{2})=10$, \\
thus, $k=\boxed{10}$.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, rectangle OABC is divided into six smaller rectangles by three lines. If D and E are the trisection points on the side CO, and the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{k}{x}\left(k\ne 0\right)$ passes through the vertices F and G of the smaller rectangles. If the area of the shaded rectangles in the figure satisfies $S_1+S_2=5$, what is the value of the inverse proportionality constant $k$?
raw_record.answer: \textit{Solution}: Since D and E are the trisection points on side CO, it follows that $S_1+S_2=\frac{1}{3}S_{\text{rectangle }OABC}$, hence $S_{\text{rectangle }OAGD}=\frac{2}{3}S_{\text{rectangle }OABC}$, therefore $S_{\text{rectangle }OAGD}=2(S_1+S_2)=10$, thus $k=\boxed{10}$.
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is rectangle OABC in the first quadrant, O is at the origin, OA is on the x-axis, OC is on the y-axis, and B is the upper right corner. Two horizontal lines pass through points D and E on the left side CO, trisecting CO; one vertical line passes through point F on the upper side CB, dividing the rectangle into left and right columns. Point G is on the right side AB, and is on the same horizontal line as D. The shaded part S1 is the small rectangle at the lower left, and the shaded part S2 is the small rectangle in the middle on the right side. The inverse proportional function curve y=k/x passes through F and G. Reasoning: Let OA=a, OC=c, and the x-coordinate of the vertical dividing line be t. Because D and E are trisection points of CO, the y-coordinate of E is c/3, and the y-coordinate of D is 2c/3. From the figure, F=(t,c), G=(a,2c/3). F and G are both on y=k/x, so their coordinate products are equal: tc=a·2c/3, therefore t=2a/3. Thus the width of the left column is 2a/3, the width of the right column is a/3, and the height of each row is c/3. The shaded area S1=(2a/3)(c/3)=2ac/9, S2=(a/3)(c/3)=ac/9, so S1+S2=ac/3=5, obtaining ac=15. Finally k=x_G y_G=a·2c/3=2ac/3=10.
